title.value: Mining Action Rules for Defect Reduction Planning
title.justification: The title is clearly mentioned at the beginning of the paper, alongside the authors' names and affiliations.
title.quote: Khouloud Oueslati, Gabriel Laberge, Maxime Lamothe, and Foutse Khomh. 2024. Mining Action Rules for Defect Reduction Planning.

analysis.description: The paper proposes a novel approach called CounterACT that uses Counterfactual Action Rule Mining to generate defect reduction plans without relying on black-box machine learning models. CounterACT is evaluated against existing approaches for its effectiveness in generating actionable and plausible plans for defect reduction in software projects.

type.justification: The paper involves experimentation and comparison of CounterACT with other existing approaches, focusing on practical evaluations of its effectiveness using datasets from software projects.
type.quote: We compare the effectiveness of CounterACT with the original action rule mining algorithm and six established defect reduction approaches on 9 software projects.

name.justification: The paper focuses on defect reduction planning within the context of software quality assurance and maintenance, which is a key area within Software Engineering.
name.quote: Defect reduction planning plays a vital role in enhancing software quality and minimizing software maintenance costs.

name.justification: The paper discusses explainable AI for software engineering and emphasizes the explainability of the CounterACT approach compared to black-box models.
name.quote: By training a black box machine learning model and “explaining” its predictions, explainable AI for software engineering aims to identify the code characteristics that impact maintenance risks.

name.justification: The main focus of the paper is on defect reduction planning using action rules, within the context of software quality.
name.quote: We introduce CounterACT, a Counterfactual ACTion rule mining approach that can generate defect reduction plans.

name.justification: CounterACT is the proposed approach introduced by the authors as a novel method for defect reduction planning using action rule mining.
name.quote: Based on this idea, we propose CounterACT, an approach that provides counterfactual explanations based on Action Rule Mining (ARM).

is_contributed.justification: CounterACT is introduced as a new contribution by the authors in this paper.
is_contributed.quote: In this paper, we introduce CounterACT, a Counterfactual ACTion rule mining approach.

is_executed.justification: The paper focuses on the methodology and evaluation of CounterACT on existing data rather than real-time execution on computational hardware.
is_executed.quote: Our experiments show that the combination of LLMs and planning can lead to enhanced guidance.

is_compared.justification: CounterACT is compared against various defect reduction approaches at both the release and commit levels.
is_compared.quote: We compare the effectiveness of CounterACT with the original action rule mining algorithm and six established defect reduction approaches.

referenced_paper_title.justification: There is no specific referenced title mentioned for the CounterACT model, as it is an original contribution of this paper.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Based on this idea, we propose CounterACT, an approach that provides counterfactual explanations based on Action Rule Mining (ARM).

name.value: Apache Open-Source Projects dataset by Jureczko et al.
name.justification: The dataset is mentioned in the context of the experiments conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of CounterACT.
name.quote: To conduct our study, we use a publicly available defect dataset used in previous work [27, 45] to support verifiability and foster replicability. The data consists of 9 Apache open-source projects collected by Jureczko et al [21] as described in Table 2.

referenced_paper_title.value: Towards Identifying Software Project Clusters with Regard to Defect Prediction (PROMISE ’10)
referenced_paper_title.justification: The reference to the dataset's original collection and description is given in the paper, linking to Jureczko et al.'s work.
referenced_paper_title.quote: The data consists of 9 Apache open-source projects collected by Jureczko et al [21] as described in Table 2.

name.justification: Used for examining CounterACT’s planning at the commit level, leveraging counterfactual-based planning at a finer granularity.
name.quote: In this section, we detail the experimental setup for examining CounterACT’s planning at the commit level, leveraging counterfactual-based planning at a finer-grained level (change-level). To conduct our study, we use the public dataset provided by PROMISE [64].

referenced_paper_title.justification: The dataset is acknowledged and directly referenced in the study.
referenced_paper_title.quote: To conduct our study, we use the public dataset provided by PROMISE [64].
